  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Joseph Toney, Acting City

  Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director; Maureen Tamuri, Interim Flaming

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 4:45 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Sections
  54956.9(d)(4), 54956.9(d)(2)(3), 54957, and 54957.6, and, with all Councilmembers
  present. He stated the Council discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took
  no reportable action.

  REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  February 14, 2025, with the amended agenda posted on February 20, 2025.

  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a
  motion to approve the agenda. The motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment on the Consent Calendar.

  Dean Wenner provided public comment on Item Nos. l.B.10. and 1.B.12.

  Andrew Sheldon provided public comment on Item No. 1.B. 12.

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  Item Nos. 1.B.5., 1.B.7., 1.B.10., 1.B.12. were pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. l.B.5., 1.B.7., 1.B.10., 1.B.12.
  The motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items

  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.

  74772—74842 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant

  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $1,797,024.28. City of Malibu payroll check number 5498 and ACH
  deposits were issued in the amount of $947,032.88.
  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the November 25, 2024
  Regular Meeting.
  4.  Annual Comprehensive Financial Report and Audit Management Letter for
  Fiscal Year 2023-24
  Recommended Action: Receive and file the Annual Comprehensive

  (ACFR) for Fiscal Year 2023-24.
  6.  Professional Services Agreements for On-Call Construction Management
  Services
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Professional
  Services Agreements with Filippin Engineering and Z&K Consultants to
  provide On-Call Construction Management Services.
  8.  Investment Report for‘the Month Ending January 3 1, 2025
  RecommendedAction: Receive the Investment Report for the month ending
  January 31, 2025.
  9.  Confirmation of the Director of Emergency Services Order Relating to the
  Palisades Fire Recovery
  Recommended Actionf'Confirm the Order of the Director of Emergency
  Services dated February 13, 2025 directing law enforcement to set up and
  police resident—only access checkpoints at specified roads in response to the
  Palisades Fire recovery.

  11.  Emergencv Public Works Agreement
  Recommended Action: 1) Receive a report on the approval of emergency
  Public Works agreement with Stacy and Witbeck, Inc. for emergency
  repairs in order to immediately preserve public safety; and 2) Authorize the
  City Manager or designee to amend the approved agreements if necessary
  to receive reimbursement from FEMA or any other governmental agency.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  5.  Amendment to Agreement with California Highway Patrol
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute an amendment to
  an agreement with the California Highway Patrol (CHP) for traffic
  enforcement services. Mayor Stewart l Councilmember Uhring 2

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Stewart moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion to
  authorize the Mayor to execute an amendment to an agreement with the
  California Highway Patrol (CHP) for traffic enforcement services. The
  motion carried unanimously.

  General Plan Safety Element Update
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute a professional
  services agreement with Atlas Planning Solutions to update the Safety
  Element of the General Plan.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Stewart seconded a motion
  to authorize the Mayor to execute a professional services agreement with
  Atlas Flaming Solutions to update the Safety Element of the General Plan.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  The motion carried unanimously.

  10.  Professional Services Agreements for Rebuild Consulting Services
  Recommended Action: l) Authorize the Mayor to execute individual
  Professional Services Agreements for Fire Recovery and Rebuild contract
  planning services from: A) 4Leaf, Inc., B) California Coastal Works, LLC,
  C) Interwest Group, Inc., and D) Michael Baker International, Inc.; and 2)
  Authorize the City Manager or designee to amend any of the approved
  agreements if necessary to receive reimbursement from FEMA or any other
  governmental agency.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a
  motion to: 1) authorize the Mayor to execute individual Professional

  Services Agreements for Fire Recovery and Rebuild contract planning
  services from: A) 4Leaf, Inc., B) California Coastal Works, LLC, C)
  Interwest Group, Inc, and D) Michael Baker International, Inc.; and 2)
  authorize the City Manager or designee to amend any of the approved
  agreements if necessary to receive reimbursement from FEMA or any other

  12.  Letter to Governor Newsom Requesting Support for Addressing
  Environmental Impacts Post-Fire
  Recommended Action: l) Authorize the Mayor to execute a letter
  requesting a State Executive Order to assist with dangerous conditions post-
  fire; and 2) Direct staff to submit the letter to Governor Newsom’s office.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a
  motion to: l) authorize the Mayor to execute a letter requesting a State
  Executive Order to assist with dangerous conditions post—fire; 2) directed
  staff to revise the letter in a form approved by the City Manager and City
  Attorney to add language requesting aid for other area that may impact the
  watershed and specifically requesting aid from the Army Corp ofEngineers;
  and 2) direct staff to submit the letter to Governor Newsom’s office. The
  motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRE SENTATIONS

  Presentation of Commendation to Hans Laetz and Diane Laetz in Recognition of
  KBUU’s 10th Anniversary

  Mayor Stewart presented the commendation to Hans Laetz and Diane Laetz.

  Hans Laetz thanked the Council and discussed the history of KBUU.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Acting City Manager Toney reported that the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has
  completed the first property cleanup of Phase 2 in Malibu. He encouraged residents
  to submit the Right of Entry (ROE) forms for debris removal. He reported that the
  National Guard is currently assisting the city by monitoring entry points into
  residential neighborhoods along Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) and staff is working
  with partner agencies on extending their deployment. He announced the Rebuild
  Center would open on March 10, 2025 and resources for rebuilding and recovery
  at maliburebuilds.org. He announced upcoming meetings including a Debris
  Removal Townhall on February 26, 2025, a special City Council meeting on
  February 27, 2025, a small business recovery webinar on February 28, 2025, a
  special City Council meeting on March 4, 2025 to introduce the Fire Rebuild
  ordinance, a Building Professional Townhall on March l2, 2025, and an Southern
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 24, 2025
  Page 6 of 13

  California Edison (SCE) utility undergrounding meeting on March 12, 2025.

  Detective Shien, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, provided an update on a
  DUI fatality case. He announced that the individual involved in a fatal crash on
  July 4th last year after leaving Nobu, had surrendered to authorities on an arrest
  warrant and been released on bond. He stated the court date was set for March 17,
  2025.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, presented the
  monthly crime statistics and stated there 24 Part 1 crimes in January, down from
  the previous year, likely due to the fire. He reported six cases of sea lines washing
  up on Malibu beaches due to an ongoing algae bloom and urged residents to call
  the California Wildlife Center if they encounter sick sea lions. He stated Pacific
  Coast Highway (PCH) remains open only to residents of burn zones and essential
  personnel, with passes being issued at City Hall. He discussed the placement of the
  checkpoint on PCH and explained that its current location was necessary for
  Visibility and safety near fire-damaged homes.

  The Council directed questions to staff regarding Phase 2 debris removal.

  ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

C:  Jeff Heller discussed recent public meetings and thanked the Council for their
  service. He offered his assistance with rebuilding as a former elected official and
  a contractor.

  Benjamin Donner, American Red Cross, discussed assistance from the American
  Red Cross and encouraged everyone impacted by the fire to register for support.
  He stated February 26, 2025 was the deadline to apply for immediate assistance.

  Barbara Bruderlin, Palibu Chamber of Commerce, discussed financial devastation
  of the fire to local businesses. She requested a commercial eviction moratorium,
  and discussed rent increases for some local businesses. She announced the
  Chamber was accepting donations to support businesses. She discussed resources
  to support businesses and individuals in Chamber newsletter.

  Kevin Keegan discussed preparations for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles and
  the importance of innovation to rebuild the City after the fire. He thanked non-
  profits for supporting the community.

  Gene Arnold discussed his history with the City and tragedies over the last few
  years. He requested a one-year commercial eviction moratorium.

  Norm Haynie discussed water flow in wildfires and limits of the water district tank
  capacities. He discussed private tanks and using pools for water supply in
  emergencies. He discussed challenges getting tanks permitted by water and fire.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 24, 2025
  Page 7 of 13

Dean Wenner discussed ROES and the volume of incomplete ROEs that could delay
debris removal. He expressed concerns regarding the draft rebuild ordinance.

Interim City Attorney Rusin clarified the cements at the Planning Commission
meeting.

Mr. Wenner discussed concerns regarding discretionary decisions for rebuilds and
indicated support for self-certification. He discussed the emergency provisions of
the Brown Act.

Paul Grisanti discussed the accelerated debris removal for Palisades Fire. He
discussed water system improvements that were approved and have not been
completed. He asked if septic system upgrades would be mandatory for rebuilds.

DNA Moore discussed losing her home in the Woolsey Fire and challenges
rebuilding from the fire. She discussed a Los Angeles Times article that reported
63% of Woolsey damaged properties that have not rebuilt.

Mike Moore discussed promises to streamline processes for rebuilding after the
Woolsey Fire and the many obstacles that still exist.

Raymond Portela declined the opportunity to speak.

Martin Mervel discussed potential alternative construction methods to expedite
rebuilding, including using tetrapods to stabilize segments of the shoreline.

Scott Dittrich discussed the February 27 Special meeting and encouraged everyone
to bring new ideas to rebuilding. He discussed the importance of home hardening
and designing homes to survive fires. He questioned who ROEs should be
submitted to.

Steven Hakim thanked the Councilmembers for their service to the community. He
discussed challenges for local businesses and requested more assistance for
businesses. He discussed a proposal to repurpose vacant office space for residential
units.

Luis Tena discussed cost, quality, and time factors in the rebuilding processes. He
discussed ways to improve the rebuild process to shorten the rebuild timeline.

Andrew Weyman deferred time to Terry Davis.

Terry Davis, Big Rock Mesa Property Owner Association, discussed a petition and
proposal for Program Director for Fire Rebuilds. She proposed Abe Roy for the
Program Director position.

Daniel Ralston deferred time to Jefferson Wagner.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 24, 2025
  Page 8 of 13

Jefferson Wagner discussed Woolsey rebuild stats, resources the City needs to
rebuild, and ways to improve the permitting process. He indicated support for a
Rebuild Czar.

Lester Tobias discussed the importance of getting the Local Coastal Program
Amendment (LCPA) for f1re rebuilds submitted to the California Coastal
Commission (CCC) as soon as possible. He made suggestions on how to process
correspondence to expedite the finalization of the ordinance.

Megan Lorick discussed her issues getting emergency notifications during the
Palisades Fire. She expressed concern regarding the timeline for rebuilding and
indicated support for Terry Davis” comments. She discussed the need for a f1re
prevention plan, MRCA brush clearance, and the need to improve Fire Department
response to future fires.

Christopher Sorensen indicated support for Lester Tobias’s comments. He
suggested roof sprinklers and other fire resiliency requirements be implemented.
He discussed streamlining the permitting and rebuilding process through systemic
processes. He suggested installing a sewer system for properties on PCH.

Arno Koch discussed the rebuild timeline and the impacts of any delays. He
discussed like-for-like rebuild requirements and stated foundation slabs and
assessor sketches should be sufficient to document what was previously built. He
discussed permitting pools as a fire safety measure.

Marcie Post, Jack Lettinger, Zach Zimmerman, Janet Fulk deferred time to Abe
Roy.

Abe Roy discussed rebuilding and challenges in Woolsey rebuild process. He
discussed a proposal for a rebuild organization structure, rebuilding workshops,
how to streamline fire rebuild application processing, advanced building
techniques, and utilizing local volunteers to collectively rebuild.

Jimmy Petulla discussed the impact disasters have on local businesses.

Ryan Embree stated the City needed a commitment from FEMA and state offlcials
to reimburse the City’s costs for recovery and rebuild. He suggested improving
water systems to increase flow in Big Rock as part of rebuilding. He discussed
undergrounding all the utilities in the City. He recommended the Council meet
every week. He suggested returning the grant for the Go Slow Malibu campaign
due to delays from fire impacts. He discussed emergency siren towers.

Jo Drummond discussed PCH access and delays and confusion about debris
removal. She suggested maintaining fire breaks created by the fire and using goats
for brush clearance.

Jaime discussed his experience rebuilding from Woolsey Fire. He discussed the
   Malibu City Council
  Minutas of February 24, 2025
  Page 9 of 13

  importance of applying exemptions for the Palisades Fire to Woolsey Fire
  properties. He discussed temporary housing requirements during rebuilding. He
  discussed the importance of improving brush clearance practices.

  Jed August requested an emergency order from the Governor to allow fire debris to
  be taken to a designated debris site in Calabasas. He discussed hazards from debris
  removal process and health hazards from exposed septic systems. He encouraged
  the public to request a reduction to their property tax bill.

RECESS  At 8:05 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:26
  pm. with all Councilmembers present.
ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Conrad discussed the importance of supporting local businesses
  and meetups she is hosting at local businesses. She indicated support for
  considering a commercial eviction moratorium. She announced she would be
  donating her City Council salary to small businesses. She discussed the challenges
  to supporting small businesses.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Attorney Rusin clarified the
  requirements for an emergency City Council meeting under the Brown Act.

  Councilmember Conrad requested more information on Water District No. 29.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Acting City Manager Toney discussed
  plans for a Special meeting on February 27, 2025 to discuss topics requested by the
  Council on February 10, 2025.

  Councilmember Conrad discussed emergency warning sirens. She discussed a
  meet up at Aviator Nation and the value of meeting directly with the residents.

  Councilmember Silverstein restated he understood the rebuild items would be heard
  tonight, but they had been scheduled for the February 27, 2025.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Acting City Manager Toney listed items
  for Thursday agenda.

  Councilmember Silverstein requested consensus to discuss the format for the
  March 4, 2025 meeting on February 27, 2025.

  The Council discussed scheduling an item to provide direction on the formation for
  the March 4, 2025 special meeting.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item at the February 27,
  2025 Special meeting to consider the format of the March 4, 2025 Special meeting.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 24, 2025
  Page 10 of 13

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the most recent Flaming Commission
  meeting and the Assistant City Attorney’s advice to the Flaming Commissioners
  limiting their comments during the meeting. He discussed the role of the City
  Attorney to provide legal advice. He requested consensus to bring back an item on
  February 27 to consider scheduling workshops before considering the fire rebuild
  Local Coastal Plan Amendment and Malibu Municipal Code Amendments.

  The Council discussed scheduling an item to consider scheduling workshops the
  fire rebuild Local Coastal Plan Amendment and Malibu Municipal Code
  Amendments.

  CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item at the February 27,
  2025 Special meeting to consider scheduling workshops for the fire rebuild Local
  Coastal Plan Amendment and Malibu Municipal Code Amendments.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the nonprofit Samaritan's Purse assisting
  residents with sifting debris. He requested consensus to bring back an item on the
  budget for programs to address homelessness and suggested using that budget to
  assist individuals experiencing homelessness due to the Palisades Fire.

  The Council discussed the timeline for the budget and when to discuss the
  homelessness budget.

  CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring an item to the Administration and
  Finance Subcommittee to discuss the budget for programs to address homelessness.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the city’s complex permit process and the
  importance of streamlining rebuild permitting for like-for-like rebuilds as much as
  possible. He discussed how the Governor’s Executive Orders could expedite
  rebuilding for the Palisades Fire. He suggested an ombudsman help review
  challenging applications. He stated the ROE forms needed to be filed with the
  County.

  Councilmember Uhring encouraged the public to participate in upcoming meetings
  related to rebuilding. He discussed the Planning Commission meeting and the large
  number of speakers. He discussed the importance of considering safety with
  rebuilding.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Acting City Manager Toney stated the
J  recruitment for the Community Development Director would be open soon.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated he
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 24, 2025
  Page 11 of 13

  could look into the legal recruitment requirements.

  Councilmember Uhring stated the Army Corps of Engineers had a customer service
  trailer on Civic Center Way. He discussed truck traffic on Malibu Canyon from
  debris removal.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins encouraged everyone to contact the Red Cross if they
  needed support. She discussed support local businesses by shopping and eating
  local. She stated the ROE application would be live on Wednesday. She discussed
  the maliburebuildsorg website and the rebuilding permit options currently
  available. She encouraged property owners to start working with their design
  professionals and meeting with staff. She encouraged the public to attend the public
  meetings and town halls.

  Mayor Stewart discussed tax reductions for fire damaged properties. He
  encouraged property owners to file the ROE forms by the March 3 1, 2025 deadline.
  He encouraged property owners to make an informed decision when deciding to
  keep their foundation during debris removal. He discussed challenges with self—
  certification permits. He stated Phase l Debris Removal was almost complete. He
  discussed challenges finding sites for debris removal. He announced dial—a—ride
  had been approved to use PCH to take seniors to doctor appointments in Santa
  Monica. He discussed efforts to get the bus line running again. He discussed the
  traffic from debris removal. He discussed Red Cross resources for emergency
  housing for those displaced by the fire. He discussed the importance of making
  improvements to systems and not just approving funding. He discussed the
  Planning and Building Safety requirements for a permit and how the Governor’s
  Executive Orders and the LCPA for fire rebuilds would exempt rebuild permits
  from most Planning requirements. He discussed Woolsey Fire rebuild statistics.

ITEM 5  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None.

ITEM 6  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 7  NEW BUSINESS

  Malibu Little League Fee Waiver
  Recommended Action: Consider whether to approve the request from Malibu Little
  League to waive the field use and snack shack equipment rental fees for the 2025
  baseball and softball season.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 24, 2025
  Page 12 of 13

  Speaker: John Alfono

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a motion to
  approve the request from Malibu Little League to waive the field use and snack
  shack equipment rental fees for the 2025 baseball and softball season. The motion
  carried unanimously.

  B.  Naming Rights for Public Facilities
  Recommended Action: Review and provide feedback on the proposed City Council
  Policy #52 Naming Rights for Public Facilities.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

CONENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to finalize the policy and bring it back for
  adoption.

  C.  City Council Post-Disaster Additional Meetings and Communication
  Recommended Action: Discuss and provide direction on scheduling additional
  City Council meetings, community meetings, and/or other meetings and
  implementing a framework for outreach, community engagement and updates
  related to the recent flres.

  Acting City Manager Toney presented the staff report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Andrew Sheldon, Bryan Fogel, and Jo Drummond

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  Councilmember Conrad left the dais at 10:26 pm.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of F6bruary 24, 2025
  Page 13 of 13

  The Council discussed the item.

  Councilmember Conrad returned to the dais at 10:28 pm.
  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to: 1) set a schedule
  of special meetings on alternating weeks of regular City Council meetings; and 2)
  consider reorganizing the regular City Council meeting format.

  MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tern Riggins seconded a
  motion to hear Item No. 8A. after 10:30. The motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 8  COUNCIL ITEMS

  A.  Council Appointments to the Malibu Arts Commission and Public Works
  Commission
  Recommended Action: 1) Mayor Pro Tem Riggins to make an appointment to the
  Malibu Arts Commission; and 2) Councilmember Uhring to make an appointment
  to the Public Works Commission.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
J  present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  Councilmember Uhring appointed Scott Dittrich to the Public Works Commission.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins appointed Dennis Smith to the Malibu Arts Commission.

  ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Stewart adjourned the meeting at 10:38 p.m.

  Approved and adopted by the City Council of the
  City of Malibu on May 21, 2025.
